behaviors.title: Single pre-pool ownership
behaviors.required_behavior: An admitted transaction has one full-hash PrePoolKernel entry, one of the frozen seven locations and one globally non-reused version until an atomic handoff transfers sole authority to TxPool.
behaviors.hostile_case: A stale worker, duplicate admission, failed transition or ABA remove/readmit race must not create two owners, resurrect an old payload or silently erase the current owner.
reviewer_questions: Does every transition consume exactly the state and lease it proves current?
Are every queue, deadline, dependency and conflict structure derived indexes rather than payload owners?
Does failure restore the old owner or publish one explicit terminal outcome?
behaviors.performance_bound: No second owner map, compensating queue, global post-transition scan or extra hot-path lock.

behaviors.title: Authoritative commit and handoff
behaviors.required_behavior: The TxPool write guard is the only final membership/RBF sequencer. It builds one immutable PoolMutationPlan, completes the versioned kernel handoff while accepted membership is unchanged, and then performs total PoolMap Apply before stable effects are journaled.
behaviors.hostile_case: Concurrent commits, stale leases, rejected RBF, capacity failure or a structural defect must not expose a pool/kernel ownership gap, strand Ready work or publish success for an unapplied plan.
reviewer_questions: Is every final fee/conflict decision recomputed under the pool write guard?
Can any ordinary error occur after accepted-pool Apply begins?
Is an uncertain authoritative mutation escalated instead of downgraded to a transaction reject?
behaviors.performance_bound: Reuse the existing pool sequencer; do not add a normal-path recovery lock, second commit queue or population-sized reconciliation.

behaviors.title: Deterministic mutation-free RBF planning
behaviors.required_behavior: Only verified candidates participate in deterministic conflict ordering, while TxPool recomputes the complete replacement closure and both fee gates before atomic victim displacement.
behaviors.hostile_case: An under-fee, multi-input, dep-group, self-evicted or concurrent candidate must not preempt through speculative state; every failed replacement must leave the complete original pool unchanged.
reviewer_questions: Is coordinator ordering still provisional rather than an admission verdict?
Are all input and expanded dependency conflicts included in the immutable removal union?
Does every failed path preserve original statuses, accounting and descendant order?
behaviors.performance_bound: Conflict work stays within indexed bounded cohorts and immutable mutation plans; no full-pool scan under the write guard.

behaviors.title: Causal dependency graph
behaviors.required_behavior: Raw, resolved and accepted exact dependency keys—including headers and expanded dep-group members—remain one canonical primary fact: availability wakes children and definitive loss invalidates them atomically while by-parent is only a derived projection.
behaviors.hostile_case: Late-discovered parents, conditional reader/spender cycles, reversed arrival order, stale resolved children or parent replacement must not strand a child, lose its wake edge or let a template commit an invalid order.
reviewer_questions: Are input, cell-dep, header-dep and expanded dep-group roles intentionally distinguished?
Does parent success/failure update reverse edges, accounting and child location in one transition?
Are cascade size and maintenance work explicitly bounded?
behaviors.performance_bound: Use bounded indexed parent/child buckets and maintenance slices; never poll all waiting transactions or scan the pool for dependents.

behaviors.title: Conflict-history Wait ownership and wakeup
behaviors.required_behavior: Historical conflicts are ordinary bounded PrePoolKernel Wait entries until an exact dependency becomes available in the post-mutation TxPool/Snapshot overlay; waking changes the same primary owner atomically and is version-safe, while RPC projects retained conflict history through recent-reject rather than as live Pending work.
behaviors.hostile_case: A release observed before another parent becomes live, an output created and consumed in one attached branch, duplicate metadata enrichment, remote conflict pinning or high-fanout input must not lose the only future wake, create a false wake, overwrite the root rejection, masquerade as Pending, retain epoch history without a waiter, duplicate ownership or cause unbounded pool-lock work.
reviewer_questions: Does Wait retain ownership until an exact dependency epoch changes?
Does every chain/pool availability edge re-arm a previously examined entry only when the resulting authoritative overlay makes that exact dependency available?
Are discovery, generations and fanout work bounded and fair?
behaviors.performance_bound: Bound history count/bytes and process indexed recovery in fixed fair slices outside population-sized scans.

behaviors.title: Continuous hostile-state accounting
behaviors.required_behavior: Global and per-peer count, bytes and active-work budgets continuously charge payload and conservative metadata in every resident state, including bounded terminal effects.
behaviors.hostile_case: Parking, invalidation, reservation, peer churn or an oversized displacement plan must not refund resident state, including the remote/per-peer charge of conflict history, evict unrelated stronger work or mutate before proving the bound.
reviewer_questions: Is every owner charged if and only if it is resident?
Are count, bytes, graph edges, victims and active work all bounded before mutation?
Does an impossible peer admission fail before global eviction planning?
behaviors.performance_bound: Budget checks and victim selection use maintained bounded indexes; no attacker-sized repair on the admission hot path.

behaviors.title: Level-triggered executable readiness
behaviors.required_behavior: Readiness is derived after each transition from the authoritative capability-aware checkout predicate; failed ineligible checkout is silent and one supervisor per worker re-arms executable work after a panic with shared bounded backoff. Cancellation and loss of command authority are terminal.
behaviors.hostile_case: A capped peer backlog must not self-wake into mutex-starving livelock; a small-only worker must not consume the only wake for large work; cancellation, zero workers, a consumed Notify before panic or a permanently closed command channel must neither strand executable work nor create an immediate respawn loop.
reviewer_questions: Does notification mean at least one worker of this capability can execute now?
Can a consumed permit be reconstructed from authoritative state after subscribe or respawn?
Does cancellation stop checkout before another self-sustaining wake loop begins?
behaviors.performance_bound: Readiness checks inspect bounded owner heads/caps only; worker count is configuration-bounded and each worker has exactly one supervisor with bounded restart rate; no manager task, exit channel, polling loop, per-item task or queue-wide scan.

behaviors.title: Administrative and hostile-peer terminalization
behaviors.required_behavior: Ban, expiry and malformed-input policy terminalize the current non-committing owner once, release all resource/index state and publish only policy-eligible effects. Clear swaps the complete entry generation and publishes one constant-size GenerationReset, which releases all relayer filters without scanning or retaining a population-sized hash batch.
behaviors.hostile_case: An already active malicious peer must not pin an active slot, resurrect through a late lease or turn a typed malformed input into fail-stop or an ineligible relay reject.
reviewer_questions: Does administrative removal make every outstanding lease stale atomically?
Are trusted promotion and immutable ingress attribution preserved deliberately?
Are ban/reject history and relay policy separate explicit decisions?
behaviors.performance_bound: Administrative removal uses indexed owners and bounded batches; peer fences/history remain bounded and expiring.

behaviors.title: Statically partitioned stable-state effects
behaviors.required_behavior: A mutation-coupled immutable batch passes one exact static-region predicate, runs a total Apply and enters the global sequence under the journal's innermost lock; no reservation or capacity token crosses a lock or await. Remote, trusted and chain-critical regions are isolated, resident queued/active records are exactly charged, and a chain transition that cannot publish detail installs one prebuilt replaceable GenerationReset without waiting behind the FIFO.
behaviors.hostile_case: Remote saturation, a full critical FIFO, a permanently full relay endpoint, callback re-entry/panic/hang, publisher unwind, close race or check-before-wait window must not mutate without a matching authority record, consume trusted/critical progress, delay chain convergence, expose intermediate state, reorder a retained batch, lose charge, spawn unbounded workers, fail-stop the service or sleep forever.
reviewer_questions: Is the immutable batch exact before Apply, or covered by one statically proved largest-indivisible Plan bound?
Does Full/Closed/Oversize return before Apply, with the journal lock innermost and no capacity token crossing a lock or await?
Are Remote, trusted and critical usage accounted independently while queued and active, and does saturated chain detail fall back to the prebuilt reset register rather than wait?
behaviors.performance_bound: One bounded journal publisher and one bounded callback endpoint worker; O(1) admission/accounting, no per-effect task, unbounded channel, callback-under-lock or busy retry.

behaviors.title: Serialized reliable chain transitions
behaviors.required_behavior: The first retained reorg phase atomically switches snapshot/membership, transfers the complete bounded accepted descendant closure of detached producers into one charged parent-first RecoveryRetained session, then journals the immediate template reset; its trusted drainer uses ordinary admission while the independently retried second phase carries only a bounded compact-uncle token and publishes the matching final generation.
behaviors.hostile_case: Repeated phase panic, a late accepted child, startup zombie reconcile, an over-budget or over-fanout descendant closure, duplicate/colliding detached roots, clear/save races or a stale full-template retry must not drop/overtake chain authority, expose a parentless accepted suffix or unowned payload interval, retain transaction-bearing blocks outside the kernel, cross a missing parent prefix or publish stale uncles/template state.
reviewer_questions: Does the paired mutation follow TxPool then PrePoolKernel then innermost EffectJournal, with every recovery payload charged before locks open and no stateful guard crossing an await?
Can phase-two retry replay phase one, retain full detached blocks, or leave its inserted uncles after panic/supersession?
Are accepted descendants planned before startup zombie reconciliation, transferred child-first/retained parent-first, and reset as one ephemeral generation when the bounded closure cannot fit?
Are duplicate/collision handling, closure-safe truncation, full/witness identity, non-reused session/version clocks and clear epoch ordering exact?
behaviors.performance_bound: First-phase graph traversal and transfer stop at the fixed mutation/recovery bounds and use one generation reset beyond them; phase two contains at most the assembler candidate bound, with no recovery lock, independent worker, population scan or full-block duplication after phase one.

behaviors.title: Coherent persistence recovery point
behaviors.required_behavior: Under one TxPool-read then PrePoolKernel snapshot boundary, persistence copies causal-parent-first accepted entries plus every retained/leased recovery-source payload into a bounded v2 envelope, releases authority locks, and serializes atomic writers without draining live state; startup also accepts the legacy v1 vector and revalidates every transaction.
behaviors.hostile_case: Save racing detached replay/clear, an active recovery lease, malformed or oversized disk data, writer failure or expanded dep-group ordering must not persist an ownership gap, allocate from an unbounded length, lose the previous atomic file, drain the live pool or serialize children before required parents.
reviewer_questions: Does save use only the universal TxPool-read then kernel order and include accepted xor every recovery owner at one linearization point?
Is PoolMap the accepted ordering authority, including expanded dependencies, while recovery metadata preserves parent-first session order?
Are file bytes/counts bounded before allocation, writes temp-sync-rename atomic, and all startup payloads revalidated rather than trusted?
behaviors.performance_bound: Shutdown-only clone/sort work stays off admission paths; do not add a continuously maintained persistence projection.

behaviors.title: Generation-local defect containment
behaviors.required_behavior: An impossible authoritative unwind exchanges only ephemeral accepted/entry generations while the TxPool guard remains closed, preserves process-global version/session clocks, emits one prebuilt GenerationReset and keeps chain, Local, Proposal, query and mining paths live; the sealed retired accepted/kernel bundle is destroyed only after authority guards open and replenishes the single emergency spare, while Remote alone enters bounded cooling, exact-witness quarantine and circuit-open after repeated resets.
behaviors.hostile_case: A reproducible legal witness, stale pre-reset lease, session reuse, relay saturation or repeated witness variants must not cancel the tx-pool service, persist/reuse a partial generation, ABA-delete a new owner or force an endless whole-pool reset loop.
reviewer_questions: Does the swap install the target/current chain snapshot and fresh primary/index generation before either authority guard opens?
Do entry versions, recovery sessions and stable effect/template authorities survive the generation exchange?
Does the one disposal permit keep retired residency bounded and force destruction/spare replenishment outside both authority locks?
Is exact wtx quarantine/cooling absent from the healthy hot-path lock set, bounded in memory, and fail-closed only for Remote after repeated resets?
behaviors.performance_bound: Healthy admission adds no new mutex acquisition; one prebuilt spare, one prebuilt reset record and one serialized disposal permit make the impossible swap bounded without destroying population-sized graphs under authority locks.

behaviors.title: Atomic accepted-pool graph integrity
behaviors.required_behavior: Full-hash pool entries are authoritative; proposal slots, status counters, causal links, outpoint indexes, sort keys and aggregate totals are rebuildable projections changed by one immutable bounded plan and total Apply.
behaviors.hostile_case: Ghost links, short-ID collision, counter drift, late-parent insertion, expired-parent cascades or virtual self-eviction must not corrupt graph weights, preserve impossible children or partially remove accepted entries.
reviewer_questions: Does one immutable plan cover the complete mutation before any write?
Does the independent audit rebuild agree after Apply and remain unchanged after every rejection?
Are required parents distinguished from ordering-only references?
behaviors.performance_bound: Mutation and audit work is bounded by explicit graph/victim caps; cold repair must never hide hot-path drift.

behaviors.title: Block-template liveness and priority
behaviors.required_behavior: Reset and full rebuild remain mutually exclusive with full highest priority; optimistic proposal/transaction updates are revision-safe, and valid recovered transactions always regain a proposal/commit path.
behaviors.hostile_case: Detached uncle proposals, stale Gap status or an update_full race must not make a valid transaction RPC-pending but forever absent from normal get_block_template mining.
reviewer_questions: Does full/reset retain authority over every optimistic delta and re-dirty skipped generations?
Can uncle proposal filtering exclude the sole proposal path of a recovered transaction?
Are Gap/Pending/Proposed transitions reflected to assembler selection?
behaviors.performance_bound: Keep optimistic CAS updates and bounded selection; do not serialize every delta behind full rebuild or remove bounded packing safeguards without measurements.

behaviors.title: Full transaction and witness identity
behaviors.required_behavior: Ownership and duplicate boundaries use full raw hashes, proposal short IDs remain non-authoritative indexes, and verification-cache proofs are keyed only by the exact witness hash through TxVerificationCacheKey.
behaviors.hostile_case: Short-ID collisions or same-raw/different-witness variants must not alias accepted/cache/history ownership, obtain a false duplicate success or reuse an invalid verification proof during reorg.
reviewer_questions: Is a short ID used only where collision-aware lookup semantics are explicit?
Can any cache call construct a key from raw hash or arbitrary bytes?
Does reorg recovery query the exact transaction witness variant?
behaviors.performance_bound: Use compact full hashes/typed cache keys without retaining packed backing; collision handling remains indexed and bounded.

behaviors.title: Bounded attacker-controlled work
behaviors.required_behavior: Owner-head scheduling, victim selection and conflict probing stop at maintained bounds independent of unrelated population; benchmark comparisons use fingerprinted paired checkpoints and reject noisy samples.
behaviors.hostile_case: A capped peer prefix, stronger suffix or large independent population must not turn one admission/checkout into an O(pool) scan; a noisy or mismatched harness must not claim a performance win.
reviewer_questions: Is operation count bounded by owners/cohort/config rather than resident transaction count?
Did the change add allocation, lock, task, scan or mutable projection to a hot path?
When benchmarking is authorized, are worktree, binary, config, repetitions and spread comparable?
behaviors.performance_bound: Deterministic operation-count regressions are always required; timing A/B is the separately authorized final gate, never inferred from unit duration.

integration_evidence.boundary: Both reader-first and spender-first RPC arrival orders retain the valid pair; normal get_block_template deterministically places the cell-dep reader before the spender and commits both.
Two thousand cell-dep readers coexist with a spender without becoming persistent ancestors, while a genuine causal chain still stops at the configured ancestor limit.
A detached dependent tree is recovered as real Pending and is re-proposed and committed by normal get_block_template mining without relying on optional uncles or a hand-authored proposal block.
A three-level detached dependency chain is replayed parent-first and every member returns to a committable pool state after the node adopts the competing fork.
A detached parent and its dependent child are both recovered through the node reorg callback and remain committable as one dependency-ordered pool graph.

When a formerly committed parent is detached while its child and grandchild remain accepted, the node transfers the complete accepted closure into parent-first recovery, restores all three as Proposed and retains the ordinary dead-input conflict verdict.
Replacing a Proposed transaction rejects the victim, refreshes the real node template, and normally proposes and commits only the replacement.
When a replacement frees only one of two historical inputs, the node recovers exactly the newly eligible victim and retains the still-conflicting victim as rejected.

The node enforces the replacement fee rule, exposes the victim as RBFRejected, commits the accepted higher-fee replacement, and does not reinterpret an output created and consumed in that attached branch as an availability edge that overwrites the root rejection.
A higher-fee replacement of a Proposed chain member survives a subsequent blank block, is freshly proposed, and is committed while the displaced closure remains rejected.
Concurrent RPC submissions for one input converge to the unique highest-fee transaction and record every losing candidate as rejected without a recovery livelock.
A cyclic sequence of overlapping replacements recovers the transaction whose input becomes free and does not resurrect transactions whose inputs remain consumed.
Final node admission rejects a replacement that depends on a cell from its victim closure and records the failed candidate without corrupting the accepted pool graph.
